claims.text: Refractory alloying-element powders and copper tend to segregate because of a significant positive heat of mixing.
SPS can be used to consolidate refractory high-entropy-alloy powders into a sintered bulk material.
SPS will enable a rapid in situ reaction between refractory high-entropy-alloy elements and copper.
The proposed SPS reaction is suitable for large-scale processing.
SPS will minimize phase segregation in the refractory-alloy–copper system.
SPS will yield a stable refractory-alloy–copper composite microstructure suitable for high-temperature nuclear-reactor applications.
The proposed SPS process requires a high heating rate, high pressure, and an optimized temperature dwell time.
A protective or controlled atmosphere can be used during SPS processing of an RHEA.
SPS parameters can be selected to generate reaction kinetics fast enough to suppress phase separation.
The process will form an in situ composite in which refractory elements and copper are uniformly integrated.
The high heating rate and pressure of SPS reduce the time available for diffusion-driven segregation.
Limiting segregation time promotes a rapid homogeneous reaction and stabilizes the composite microstructure.
The SPS composite will have enhanced microstructural and phase stability.
The SPS composite will have better high-temperature performance than a conventionally sintered composite.
Traditional sintering uses slower heating rates that permit segregation and unstable microstructure formation through prolonged diffusion.
The proposed benefits apply primarily to combinations of refractory alloying elements and copper.
The efficacy of the SPS route may vary with alloy composition and processing scale.
The quantitative improvements in microstructural stability and mechanical properties have not been established.
